scientific.title: Scientific
scientific.description: Trigonometry, logarithms, complex numbers and configurable precision.
scientific.keyboardHint: Use Enter to calculate, Shift+Enter for a new line and Escape to cancel.
scientific.precisionError: Enter a working precision from 8 to 80 digits.

algebra.title: Algebra
algebra.description: Rewrite expressions, solve equations and check candidate solutions.
algebra.keyboardHint: Use Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate and Escape to cancel.
algebra.rejected: Candidate is outside the solution set
algebra.allReal: Every real x is a solution
algebra.allComplex: Every complex x is a solution

hints.simplify: Enter a rational expression in x, y or z. Excluded values appear with the answer.
hints.expand: Use parentheses to group factors and ^ to enter powers.
hints.factor: Enter a polynomial in one variable with rational coefficients.
hints.polynomial: The result lists coefficients from highest to lowest degree.
hints.solve: Enter an equation in one variable and choose the solution domain.
hints.inequality: Enter an inequality in one variable using <, ≤, > or ≥.
hints.system: Place each linear equation on a new line or separate equations with semicolons.
hints.substitute: Enter the expression first, followed by assignments separated by semicolons.
hints.verify: Enter the equation first, followed by candidate assignments separated by semicolons.

calculus.title: Calculus
calculus.description: Differentiate, integrate, find limits and build Taylor series.
calculus.keyboardHint: Use Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate and Escape to cancel.

proof.workingPrecision: Working precision is not a certified error bound.
proof.limitFormula: lim f(x) from each requested side
proof.entireSeries: Taylor series converges for every real input.
proof.localSeries: Taylor series converges in a neighborhood of the expansion point.

methods.limit: Leading terms on each side of the limit

hints.derivative: Choose a variable for a partial derivative. Other variables are held constant.
hints.antiderivative: Find a symbolic antiderivative when supported. The result includes the integration constant C.
hints.integral: Use finite bounds such as 0 or 1/2. This operation looks for an exact result.
hints.limit: Use a rational approach point, +∞ or −∞. At a finite point, choose a direction or compare both sides.
hints.series: Use a rational expansion point. The O term indicates the order of the omitted terms.
hints.numerical_integral: Enter finite bounds and a tolerance from 1e-12 to 1e-3. The calculation gives an approximation and an error estimate.

linearAlgebra.title: Linear algebra
linearAlgebra.description: Edit matrices and vectors, solve linear systems, and inspect factorizations and spectra.
linearAlgebra.keyboardHint: Use the arrow keys to move between cells, Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate, and Escape to cancel.
linearAlgebra.gridHint: Empty cells are zero. Paste a rectangular block with tab- or space-separated columns.
linearAlgebra.invalidCell: Enter one number or fraction per cell, with no spaces.
linearAlgebra.invalidMatrix: Check the entries. Use integers, decimals, scientific notation or fractions.
linearAlgebra.singular: Matrix A is singular and has no inverse.
linearAlgebra.eigenvectorList: Eigenvectors by column, in eigenvalue order
linearAlgebra.invalidBlock: Paste a rectangular block with the same number of columns on each row.

hints.add: A and B must have the same dimensions.
hints.subtract: A and B must have the same dimensions.
hints.multiply: The number of columns in A must match the number of rows in B.
hints.transpose: Exchange rows and columns of A.
hints.determinant: A must be square. A zero determinant indicates a singular matrix.
hints.inverse: A must be square and nonsingular.
hints.rank: Count the independent rows or columns of A.
hints.dot: Enter two row or column vectors with the same number of entries.
hints.cross: Enter two row or column vectors with three entries each.
hints.solve: Enter the coefficients in A and the right-hand side as a vector in B.
hints.eigenvalues: A must be real, square and symmetric. Results are in ascending order.
hints.eigenvectors: A must be real, square and symmetric. Each vector corresponds to an eigenvalue.
hints.lu: Factor A with row pivoting. The result satisfies P × A = L × U.
hints.qr: Factor A as Q × R. The columns of Q are orthonormal.

proof.workingPrecision: Working precision is not a certified error bound.
proof.illConditioned: Ill-conditioned: small perturbations may change the factors or solutions.
proof.clusteredEigenvalues: Closely spaced eigenvalues can make individual eigenvectors sensitive.
proof.nearZeroEigenvalue: An eigenvalue is close to zero relative to the matrix scale.
proof.realParameters: Free parameters range over the reals.
proof.zeroEigenvalue: A zero diagonal eigenvalue makes the matrix singular.
proof.rankDeficient: Rank deficient: rows or columns are linearly dependent.
proof.conditionUnavailable: Condition estimate unavailable within the iteration budget.

methods.exact_linear_system: Exact reduction of a linear system

geometry.title: Geometry
geometry.description: Find lengths, areas, volumes and relationships between points and segments.
geometry.keyboardHint: Use Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate and Escape to cancel.
geometry.invalid: Enter valid measurements or coordinate rows.
geometry.domainError: Check positive lengths, triangle inequalities, distinct points and the required shape.
geometry.projection: Coordinate diagram projected onto the x–y plane

hints.rectangle: Enter the width and length in the same unit.
hints.triangle: Enter three positive sides. The sum of any two must exceed the third.
hints.polygon: Enter 3–32 points in boundary order. Write x y on each line or use semicolons between points.
hints.sphere: Enter a positive radius for the sphere.
hints.cylinder: Enter the base radius and perpendicular height of the cylinder.
hints.cone: Enter the base radius and perpendicular height of the right cone.
hints.prism: Enter the height and 3–32 points for the simple polygonal base. Write x y on each line.
hints.distance: Enter two rows of x y or x y z coordinates.
hints.angle: Enter three rows of x y or x y z coordinates. The middle point is the vertex.
hints.segments: Enter four rows of x y coordinates. The first two points form one segment and the last two form the other.

methods.exact_vector_angle: Angle from the vector dot product

proof.inequality: The sum of any two sides exceeds the third.
proof.simplePolygon: The polygon is simple and has nonzero area.
proof.rationalLength: Positive rational length from the input

discrete.title: Discrete Mathematics
discrete.description: Count arrangements, compare sets, evaluate propositions and work with exact integers.
discrete.keyboardHint: Use Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate and Escape to cancel.
discrete.repetitionHint: Enter the multiplicity of each distinct item, separated by spaces.
discrete.invalid: Check the inputs and their separators.
discrete.domainError: Check that the values lie in the operation’s domain.
discrete.probableExplanation: A fixed set of strong Miller–Rabin tests supports the probable-prime classification.

hints.permutations: Arrange n elements in order. Use n from 0 to 4096.
hints.arrangements: Choose k ordered positions from n elements. Use n and k from 0 to 4096.
hints.combinations: Choose k elements from n without regard to order. Use n and k from 0 to 4096.
hints.set_union: Separate elements in each set with spaces. Use integers or case-sensitive ASCII labels.
hints.set_intersection: Separate elements in each set with spaces. Use integers or case-sensitive ASCII labels.
hints.set_difference: Find the elements in A that are absent from B.
hints.set_symmetric_difference: Find the elements that belong to exactly one set.
hints.set_subset: Check whether every element of A belongs to B. A blank field represents an empty set.
hints.logic: Use the logic symbols and names such as A or event_1. Assign variables with entries such as A=1 B=0.
hints.truth_table: Use the logic symbols and up to eight variable names. Each row shows the resulting truth value.
hints.prime: Enter a signed integer. Values above the unsigned 64-bit range use a bounded probable-prime test.
hints.factor: Enter a nonzero signed integer with magnitude within the unsigned 64-bit range.
hints.modular: Use a positive modulus. An inverse or a negative exponent requires a coprime value and modulus.
hints.sequence: Use a zero-based index from 0 to 32768.

methods.exact_lcm_via_gcd: Least common multiple via the GCD

proof.primeDomain: Integers greater than one can be prime.
proof.factors: Prime factors verified with multiplicity in the unsigned 64-bit range.
proof.inverseModulus: A modular inverse requires coprime operands and a modulus above one.
proof.zeroBased: The sequence index starts at zero.

programmer.title: Programmer
programmer.description: Convert between number bases and inspect fixed-width bit operations.
programmer.keyboardHint: Use Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate and Escape to cancel.
programmer.invalid: Enter digits for the selected base and a decimal count.
programmer.domainError: The value must fit the selected word. Shift and rotation counts must be nonnegative.
programmer.invalidWidth: Enter a bit width between 1 and 1024.
programmer.wordPolicy: Use 1–1024 bits. Unsigned binary, octal and hexadecimal literals encode bit patterns. The signed setting interprets the leading bit as the sign.

hints.convert: Enter one value in the selected input base.
hints.and: Keep positions where both bits are 1.
hints.or: Set positions where either bit is 1.
hints.xor: Set positions where the two bits differ.
hints.not: Flip every bit within the selected width.
hints.shift_left: Shift left and fill from the right with zeros. Excess bits are discarded.
hints.shift_right_logical: Shift right and fill from the left with zeros.
hints.shift_right_arithmetic: Shift right and repeat the leading bit from the left in either interpretation.
hints.rotate_left: Wrap bits around the left end of the word. Enter a decimal count.
hints.rotate_right: Wrap bits around the right end of the word. Enter a decimal count.
hints.twos_complement: Negate the word modulo 2 raised to the selected bit width.

proof.exactCount: Exact decimal count from the input
proof.shiftLimit: The shift count reaches or exceeds the word width.
proof.leftWrap: A left shift discards bits beyond the word width.
proof.logicalFill: A logical right shift fills with zeros.
proof.arithmeticFill: An arithmetic right shift repeats the leading bit.
proof.twosWrap: Two’s complement negation wraps modulo 2 raised to the word width.
proof.minSigned: The smallest signed value retains its bit pattern.

converter.title: Converter
converter.description: Convert compatible units or apply a dated exchange rate from your records.
converter.keyboardHint: Use Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate and Escape to cancel.
converter.invalid: Enter a valid amount and check the selected units or rate details.
converter.domainError: Check the amount and conversion constraints, including absolute zero, positive fuel economy and the validity period.
converter.manualHint: Enter a positive rate, its source, the rate date and the reference date you want to evaluate. The expiry date is optional.

hints.length: Enter a length as a number or fraction.
hints.volume: Choose two volume units. US and imperial measures are distinct.
hints.temperature: Convert a measured temperature. Zero points and absolute-zero limits apply.
hints.temperature_delta: Convert a temperature interval using scale factors. Differences can be negative.
hints.pressure: Pressure factors are exact where defined. The nominal mmHg factor is approximate.
hints.power: Choose two power units. Mechanical and metric horsepower differ.
hints.angle: Convert an angle. Exact results can contain π.
hints.storage: Decimal prefixes use powers of 1000 and binary prefixes use powers of 1024.
hints.transfer: Choose a unit per second. Bits and bytes have different scales.
hints.fuel: Use nonnegative values. A reciprocal conversion between distance per fuel and fuel per distance requires a positive value.

validity.within_validity: The rate is valid on the selected reference date.
validity.expired: The rate had expired by the selected reference date.
validity.not_yet_valid: The selected reference date is before the rate date.
validity.unverified_validity: Validity on the selected reference date is unverified.

constraints.Nominal result rounded to seven signific: The nominal result uses seven significant digits, with ties rounded to even.
constraints.Absolute temperature is at least zero ke: Absolute temperature is at least zero kelvin.
constraints.Reciprocal fuel conversion requires a po: The reciprocal fuel conversion requires a positive input.
constraints.Rate expressed as target currency per so: The rate gives target currency units per source currency unit.

proof.workingPrecision: Working precision is not a certified error bound.

dateTime.title: Date & Time
dateTime.description: Compare civil dates, count business days, and convert timestamp offsets and time zones.
dateTime.keyboardHint: Use Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter to calculate and Escape to cancel.
dateTime.invalid: Enter valid ISO dates or timestamps and check the calendar or time zone settings.
dateTime.domainError: Check that the dates, period and calendar settings are within the operation’s domain.
dateTime.ambiguous: This local time occurs twice. Choose the earlier or later instant, or enter another time.
dateTime.nonexistent: This local time is skipped during a transition. Enter another local time.
dateTime.workingWeekError: Select at least one working weekday.
dateTime.holidayLimit: Enter up to 23 exclusions in YYYY-MM-DD format.
dateTime.clamp: Clamp to the last valid day
dateTime.calendarHint: Select the working weekdays and enter your own exclusions. Separate dates with line breaks or commas.
dateTime.tzdbPolicy: Daylight-saving flags follow IANA rearguard data.

fields.asOf: Date at which to calculate age

hints.difference: Use two dates in YYYY-MM-DD format. The signed interval is expressed in civil days, whole weeks and remaining days.
hints.age: Enter a birth date and a date at which to calculate age. The result counts complete calendar years and months.
hints.period: Enter signed years, months, weeks or days. Calendar years and months apply before weeks and days.
hints.calendar: Enter a civil date to show its ISO weekday, week-year, week number and leap-year status.
hints.business_days: Count selected weekdays after the start date through the end date. Reversing the range changes the sign.
hints.deadline: Count days from the start date, excluding that date. Business deadlines use the selected working calendar.
hints.timezone: Enter a local timestamp such as 2024-11-03T01:30:00 and IANA time-zone names or UTC. Choose how to resolve repeated times. A skipped time requires a different local time.
hints.duration: Enter two RFC3339 timestamps with seconds and Z or a numeric UTC offset. The result is elapsed time to nanosecond precision.

methods.custom_business_deadline: Business deadline on a custom calendar

constraints.Business calendar uses only the supplied: The working calendar applies your selected weekdays and entered exclusions.
constraints.Weeks truncate toward zero with a signed: Weeks truncate toward zero with a signed remainder.
constraints.Age uses completed clamped months before: The age counts complete calendar months with month-end adjustment, then remaining days.
constraints.Business-day interval excludes the earli: The business-day interval excludes the earlier date and includes the later date.
constraints.Deadline excludes the starting day when: A nonzero deadline count excludes the starting day.
constraints.Nonexistent local times are rejected: A skipped local time requires another input.
constraints.Explicit offsets define the UTC instants: Explicit offsets define the instants in UTC.

formulas.age = completed calendar months plus rem: Age equals complete calendar months plus remaining days.
formulas.ISO week 1 contains January 4 and starts: ISO week 1 starts on Monday and contains January 4.
formulas.signed count of eligible dates in (earli: Signed count of eligible dates after the earlier date through the later date.
formulas.first date reached after abs(count) elig: Date reached after counting eligible days in the chosen direction.

operations.offlineError: The requested offline setting could not be confirmed.
operations.localeUnavailable: This language could not be loaded. Use a downloaded language or allow static downloads.
operations.storageNote: Expressions, history and saved values live in this session. Explicit preferences stay on this device.
operations.cachedAssetsNote: Clear downloaded web assets using this site's storage controls in your browser.
operations.permissionNote: Copying uses the clipboard after your action. Battery state is optional when the browser makes it available. This version requests no account, location or credentials.

operations.policyNote: Profiles tune resource use. Mathematical precision stays the same.
